particularites.text: Ultra-diversified luxury conglomerate model acting as a sector shock absorber: in H1 2026, Watches & Jewelry (+9% organic) and Wines & Spirits (+5%) largely offset the persistent weakness of Fashion & Leather Goods (-1% organic over the half, despite a return to +1% in Q2 alone).

ownership.insiderDesc: Arnault family (Bernard Arnault and his children), through its Christian Dior SE and Financière Agache holding companies - family control structure, crossing of the symbolic 50% capital threshold in February 2026 following regular purchases in the market.

items.title: The AMF fined LVMH 8 M€ for breaches of disclosure rules during the gradual build-up of its stake in Hermès between 2008 and 2010 (use of undeclared equity swaps).

items.title: French criminal investigation into the historical build-up (2008-2010) of LVMH's stake in Hermès: several Swiss intermediaries (lawyers, a notary, a wealth manager) placed under formal investigation in 2026 for aggravated breach of trust, handling of stolen goods and forgery; the heir Nicolas Puech is claiming more than 10 Md€ in court from LVMH and Bernard Arnault, alleging an organised dispossession of his Hermès shares to their benefit.
items.allegedBy: Nicolas Puech (civil complaint filed in Paris and proceedings in the United States) / Paris public prosecutor's office (criminal judicial investigation)
items.source: Reuters, FashionUnited, The Fashion Law (May-June 2026) - LVMH firmly denies any wrongdoing, referring to a "clearly coordinated press campaign"

compliance.note: No accounting fraud or investor deception identified targeting LVMH itself at this stage; the Hermès/Puech investigation concerns third-party intermediaries and the historical build-up of a stake more than fifteen years ago, with LVMH rejecting any direct involvement. The Louis Vuitton trademark dispute raised in the H1 2026 Q&A (litigation with a tea company) and the Loro Piana subcontracting case in Italy (placed under judicial administration over labour-law matters) are deliberately excluded from this field: they are respectively an ordinary intellectual property dispute and an ESG/labour-law issue, not an allegation of fraud against investors or consumers in the sense used here.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance (LVMH does not issue formal quarterly targets). Directional message for Q3/H2: continued sequential improvement expected; the H2 comparison base is 'optically tougher' but management views it as broadly comparable once adjusted for the easy 2024 comps it mirrors; Middle East exit rate at end-Q2 still negative but much more muted, with gradual steady improvement; July too early to read.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No quantified full-year revenue or margin target. Directional FY26 guidance from the call: full-year FX impact on EBIT expected around EUR -1bn (similar to 2025, ~EUR 0.7bn already absorbed in H1), with the H2 margin hit similar to H1's despite a possible slight FX tailwind on revenue (offset by DFS disposal perimeter effects); Wines & Spirits expected to grow at constant currencies in 2026 but more moderately than H1's +5%, with full-year divisional EBIT margin close to 2025 levels (cost phasing and delayed FX impact through inventories); continued cost discipline on marketing and G&A; operating leverage only expected once group organic growth reaches 3-4%; interim dividend set at EUR 5.50/share, payable December 2026.
pointsCles: Sequential inflection confirmed: group organic growth accelerated from +1% in Q1 to +3% in Q2 (~+4% excluding a 1pt Middle East conflict drag), with Fashion & Leather Goods back to +1% organic in Q2 and both Louis Vuitton and Dior in positive territory (Dior slightly above the divisional average), driven by Jonathan Anderson's creative renewal and the Monogram 130th-anniversary push.

Margin resilience through discipline, not leverage: 22.5% operating margin on just +2% organic growth was achieved via a 2% cut in marketing & selling costs and flat G&A; CFO Cecile Cabanis explicitly warned this is not a repeatable rule and that 3-4% organic growth remains the threshold for genuine operating leverage.

FX is the dominant headwind: nearly EUR 700m negative currency impact on H1 EBIT (organic EBIT up ~4%), with a similar margin hit expected in H2 (notably in Wines & Spirits via inventory lag) even though reported revenue could see a slight FX tailwind offset by DFS disposal perimeter effects.

Demand mosaic: US accelerated to +6% in Q2 (local plus returning tourists, Americans up high-single-digit in F&LG), Asian clienteles shifted spend toward Europe and Japan (explaining Asia's sequential slowdown), Chinese local and tourist demand stayed flat but increasingly clustered around shopping events, and jewelry (Tiffany and Bvlgari both mid-teens in Q2) remained the standout while standalone watches stayed slightly negative.

guidanceHistory.guidanceAnnuelle: No quantified revenue/margin target; FX effect on annual EBIT expected at ~-1 Md€ (close to 2025), Wines & Spirits margin close to 2025, continued marketing/G&A cost discipline. Interim dividend 5,50 €/share, payable on 3 December 2026.

hypothese.summary: H1 2026 confirms an exit from the trough more favourable than feared at the previous refresh: margin held at 22,5% despite organic growth still below the 3-4% threshold, Fashion & Leather Goods returns to growth in Q2, but reported revenue misses the consensus (FX/scope effect) and the Middle East and Hermès/Puech risks remain unresolved. Independent cross-check of 29/07/2026: no material divergence identified between the refresh and the official publications/transcript.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
LVMH is the diversified luxury conglomerate exiting its 2023-2025 trough progressively rather than via a sharp rebound - and S1 2026 confirmed that path more favorably than feared: revenue 38.6bn EUR (+2% organic, +3% in Q2, ~1.3bn below consensus) but operating margin held at 22.5%, well above market fears, on cost discipline management itself calls a one-off effort. The pivotal signal: Fashion & Leather Goods returned to organic growth in Q2 (+1%) after SEVEN declining quarters, on Jonathan Anderson's Dior debut and Vuitton's Monogram 130th. Watches & Jewelry (+9%, Tiffany/Bvlgari mid-teens) and Sephora keep compounding; Wines & Spirits margins rebuilt (+210bp). The conglomerate structure works as designed - divergent divisions, one resilient P&L. Middle East (-1pt) and the DFS disposals anniversary from S2 26 into 2027; FX drag ~1bn EUR on FY26 EBIT fades at current parities. France's exceptional corporate surtax caps 2026 net (ETR ~30%), unwinding from 2027 - a mechanical net-income tailwind embedded in the bridge, not in optimism.

== THESIS READ ==
- F&LG back to organic growth in Q2 after seven down quarters - the single most thesis-relevant inflection since creation; sequential improvement now four quarters long (-3% S1 25 -> +3% Q2 26).
- Margin held at 22.5% by an explicitly non-repeatable cost effort: the model keeps FY26 margin ~flat (22.1%) rather than extrapolating H1 discipline.
- Surtax mechanics: ETR 30% in 2026 then stepping down to 28% by 2030 - net income re-rates from 2027 without any operating assumption.
- Asian customer spend is migrating to Europe/Japan (Q2: US +6% sequential, Europe positive on tourism) - demand is stable underneath the geographic optics.
- Watch: Hermes stake criminal probe (Puech claims >10bn EUR) - reputational, no P&L impact identified, tracked in compliance.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Diversified conglomerate model acting as a sector shock-absorber (reconfirmed by the S1 26 divergence: W&J +9% vs F&LG -1%).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: published IFRS recurring operating income (no management 'underlying'; the S1 theoretical mark-to-market gain on the financial portfolio is excluded from the normative conversion - see ancrage mtm_financier_exclu). Bridge (c-ter): tax 30% (2026, French surtax) stepping to 28% (2030); finNet = average net debt x (Bund 3.20% + 2pts), melting as ND falls 5.3bn -> 0.3bn; MINORITIES explicit (-1,173 -> -1,660M EUR: Moet Hennessy 34% Diageo + DFS, growing with the W&S recovery - smoothness to refine at the annual report). omniumEPS now explicit (was derived): 22.42 -> 31.42 EUR. Semiannual split built (E5 ter): H1 26 ACTUAL 11.52 EUR (published net 5.7bn / 495M shares), H2 residual 10.90; NY 48/52. FY26 revenue bottom-up: S1 published + S2 at ~3% organic with net FX/perimeter ~0. Scorecard: no-guidance house - own-vintage anchor 21.82 (09/07, imperfect, re-anchor Feb 2027), history not measurable, application suspended (documented). WATCH-LIST: (1) Marc Jacobs and DFS Okinawa closings (S2 26); (2) Middle East residual drag; (3) Chinese tourist demand concentration around shopping events; (4) Hermes/Puech probe; (5) FY26 margin holding ~flat if S2 organic disappoints; (6) FY27 consensus still unidentified. Next useful refresh: Q3 revenue (mid-October).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (mid-Oct): fifth consecutive sequential improvement test; DFS/Marc Jacobs closings; surtax unwind visibility into 2027; W&J momentum (Tiffany, Bvlgari).

ancrages.moteur: The FX effect on revenue turns slightly positive in H2 2026 according to management, but is offset by the scope effect of the DFS disposals (Greater China, LAX/SFO, Okinawa) which continue in H2, leaving the reported/organic gap close to zero over the half.

Management reaffirms that Group organic growth of 3-4% is needed to genuinely lift the operating margin; below that threshold (~2,5% organic estimated for the full year), the 2026 margin is modelled as broadly flat vs 2025 rather than expanding, despite the cost discipline demonstrated in H1 (H1 2026 margin at 22,5%, above the previous refresh's fears).

The H1 2026 financial result was flattered by a mark-to-market revaluation gain on the financial investment portfolio, explicitly described by management as purely theoretical and with no translation into real profit; that gain is not carried over into the normative 2026 Net/EBIT conversion ratio, which retains a rate close to that of FY2025 (61-62%) rather than the flattered H1 2026 rate (65,6%).

omniumND projected positive across the whole horizon: normative financial charge = projected average ND x (German 10-year Bund 3,20% at 28/07/2026 + 2 pts of spread), rate recalculated at this refresh (vs the previous refresh, a Bund increase of the order of +50-70 bps reflecting the rise in European sovereign yields in 2026).

omniumND 2026 expected to decline vs FY2025 despite the seasonal peak of 8 245 M€ at end-June 2026, driven by the traditionally stronger H2 free cash flow, the balance of the Marc Jacobs disposal to WHP Global (0,85-1 Md$, closing expected end-2026) and the lapping of the DFS disposals already cashed in; continued deleveraging towards near-neutrality in 2030.

From 2027, Group organic growth is modelled above the 3-4% threshold (lapping of the Middle East conflict and of the DFS disposals, continued normalisation of Fashion & Leather Goods), allowing a gradual margin expansion towards the group's structural target.

Fashion & Leather Goods (44% of Group revenue) returns to positive organic growth in Q2 2026 (+1%) after seven consecutive quarters of decline, driven by Jonathan Anderson's creative renewal at Dior and by Monogram momentum at Vuitton; still constrained by supply-chain tensions tied to the creative transition according to management.

Exceptional French tax surcharge confirmed for fiscal year 2026 (total tax charge ~5,5 Md€, effective rate ~30% in H1 2026); assumption of a gradual normalisation of the effective rate from 2027 maintained in the absence of confirmation to the contrary from the legislator.
